Selector zero clears the active flag and SID registers. Selectors one through four load three track pointers from $1235, reset voice sequence indices and initialise SID state. Selectors at least five continue the active piece. The return writes $FF to the selector. Voice processing uses three parallel state sets and SID offsets zero, seven and fourteen.
Immediate operand of ADC at $0B1A, patched from the selector to choose one of four three-voice track sets. The following loop installs their pointers and initialises the voices.

Selects one voice, advances note duration on tempo ticks, and handles semitone rises or falls on other ticks. When a note expires, decodes the pattern commands: $FF selects the next pattern, $FE stops, $FD sets volume, $F0 upward sets tempo, $C0 upward selects an instrument, and $80 upward sets duration.

Handles pattern commands $7B for pitch sliding and $7A for delayed vibrato. Adds the track transpose to the note, reads instrument settings, writes pulse width and, for an enabled voice, its envelope and gate waveform. Advances the pattern pointer by the consumed byte count and resets note counters.

Immediate pulse-width operand of LDA at $0C79, patched from instrument byte $1250. The following code splits it into pulse low/high fields, writes envelopes and waveform and advances the pattern pointer.

Reads instrument flags and chooses a first-tick noise or pulse attack, table-driven waveform/frequency changes, or normal modulation. The waveform and frequency table operands at $0D36/$0D37 and $0D41/$0D42 are rewritten from $11ED according to the instrument.

High operand byte of the frequency-effect lookup at $0D40. Patched alongside its low byte and waveform pointer from $11ED. The following code writes the effect frequency or enters the attack and vibrato paths.

Computes the gap between adjacent note frequencies, shifts it by the instrument's depth, advances a bounded direction counter, waits out the vibrato delay, then offsets the stored pitch around its centre and writes the two SID frequency bytes.

If the voice has an arpeggio bitmask, builds its semitone offsets and cycles them to set pitch. Otherwise an active slide installs target and duration operands, computes a frequency step and applies it with the add/subtract instructions rewritten by $0FFE.
Immediate operand of ADC at $0EC0, patched from the slide-duration nibble. The following comparisons decide whether the note is inside its sliding interval.

Opcode rewritten to ADC or SBC for the high frequency byte. Applies the carry from the low-byte operation and writes the SID high frequency byte.

At the midpoint of a note duration, writes the instrument's release waveform. Advances pulse width upward to high byte $0F or downward to below eight, reversing direction at those bounds, then processes the next voice. Advances the shared tempo countdown after all three voices.
Writes zero to SID registers $D400-$D418, from volume downward to voice one's frequency low byte.

Indexes the split frequency tables at $1085/$10E6 with the voice's note number, stores the base frequency and writes both bytes to its SID voice. X is the voice index and $11CC its SID register offset.

Rotates an eight-bit mask through carry, copying the selected semitone offsets from $115E into the voice's buffer at $11CD plus its offset from $115B. Terminates the buffer with $FF and clears pitch-slide state.

Clears sprites, selects title music, builds the title from room data and waits through message 0. Clears the collision plane, restores five 134-byte object tables from their initial values, sets room $24 and two spare lives, builds the opening room and runs the appearance animation.
Reads keyboard commands for quitting, pausing and sound selection, then combines joystick and keyboard controls. Delays by $03BC and advances movement and room events.

Sets the per-pass vertical step count to six at jump phases below two or at least sixteen, four at phases two through six and eleven through fifteen, and two at phases seven through ten. Returns before the movement continuation at $1C85.

Normalises grounded movement state and checks collision probes ahead of the player at offsets zero or seven. Rejects blocked motion, otherwise increments or decrements player X by one. Continues into floor correction and room transitions.

Probes below a descending player and clears jump state on landing. Moves the player upward out of solid terrain, then wraps X at two/$39 and Y at $80/$C0 into adjacent room IDs. Saves entry coordinates except in room $45 and rebuilds the new room before writing player sprite position and animation.

Converts player X to 4*X+$38 and Y to Y+$5A, chooses standing, walking or rolling sprite frames from movement state, applies Australia inversion and enables sprites. Handles contact events for objects $43 and $41 and the right edge of room $29 before action processing.

Clears selected-object and pickup indices. Action is suppressed while moving or airborne. A fresh action scans object IDs below $3F for a visible pickup within the player's pickup rectangle, then tests fixed interaction objects for conversation and switches.

On action overlapping object $64 while its attribute differs from $87, sets that attribute and lowers objects $65-$67 until object $66 reaches Y=$8B. Object $67's mirror bit alternates during the descent. Continues through other action targets if the switch was already active or outside reach.

Object zero enters carried room four directly. Object two first gains attribute bit $80 and message $15, then pickup scanning resumes at ID three. Picking up object $0A drops carried IDs 1-$3E at the player's position, shows message $27 and removes the hole.

Coins $1A-$37 use the decimal coin collector. Other pickup IDs below $3F enter room four, with paired objects $38 upward updating the corresponding earlier object. Builds the inventory list, applies capacity two or four depending on object zero, and opens the inventory selector.

Shows the selection prompt, starts on the exit row, colours the selection and waits for left, right or action. Left and right wrap through the zero-terminated carried list. Action chooses the ID or $FF for exit, redraws the room and enters item-use dispatch.

Tests selected IDs against target objects or room IDs. Successful branches change live object fields, consume selected items through $29C1, and show their message. Cases include IDs six, $12, $14, $10, $17-$19, $16, five, three, one, four and $0C-$0F; unmatched selections continue to later uses and ordinary dropping.

Handles item nine against object $47, item eight against $49, item $0B in room $5E, and item $11 in room $36. Updates their puzzle fields and messages, consuming the selected item where the branch calls $29C1.

Blocks ordinary drops while overlapping objects $73-$7A. Item $13 is consumed with message $28. Other selected IDs erase the old foreground object layer after raster line $FA, assign the current room and a position beside the player, then redraw objects and colours.

Checks eleven object IDs and their death-message IDs, then dragon frame $7C, room-specific moving hazards and collision-plane flags. Attribute bit $20 selects fire message $2F; bit $10 selects water or lava according to room $4D. The following death path preserves the reason while running disappearance and messages.

Saves the death message, with an exception for message $35 in room $5E once object $0B is gone. Plays disappearance, generic death and reason messages, delays seven groups of 250 units and returns to title when spare lives are zero. Otherwise decrements spare lives and restores the saved entry room and coordinates.

In room $24 while object $45 remains, checks the loaf's position against the rat. The matching case removes the loaf, flags the rat and shows message $1D. The rat otherwise moves between X bounds, or leaves to the right once the loaf is consumed.

Room $35 alternates dragon mouth frames while object $10 remains. Room $33 moves the lift strip up one or down four between its Y bounds unless its switch attribute is five. Room $2D animates object $4A's Y before the four moving-platform cases.

Unless the shared dwell timer is active, scans four platform rooms and enabled attributes. Moves paired objects $73 upward by one Y unit, updates each platform height at $18F4, reverses at its initial bounds and loads a sixteen-pass dwell timer.

In room $31, draws object $50 and decides whether to approach the player's X or patrol between X=$23 and $4F. Moves two X units per pass, drops Y by eight while pursuing, cycles three shapes at $61 upward and redraws.

In room $32 on odd passes while object five remains, builds a delay counter based on player height and object $52. After count $20, moves object $51 by two, reversing below X=$37 (the even-position path reaches $36) and at $4E. When the right bound is reached with object five's attribute high bit set, removes object five and changes the rat attribute.

In rooms $28 and $36, erases seven fire pieces and moves a prefix of them up or down by two on even passes. The prefix length oscillates from zero through six. The following section arms and advances the horizontal breath effect according to room and dragon state.

In room $28 when object $46 is removed, or room $36 at the end of the fire cycle with a random result one, starts a breath sweep at $42. Counts it down by two, switches its shape to $6D after it falls below $2A, and draws the active sweep before the scenery animation and next loop pass.
Writes $FF to the live room entry of object $03D9, then clears the selected-object index to $FF. Preserves X through $034E.
Calls the object renderer at $3306 with destination offset $58, then zero, leaving the offset as set by that renderer.
Adjusts specific live object entries after the five object tables are restored: $C7BB=$80, $C735=$52, $C6A5=$FF, $C875=$0F, $C880=$0F and $C881=$0A.

When leaving vertically into room seven, redirects to $37. Room $17 and that redirected path reset player Y to $72, direction right, jumping state and phase, with duration $11. Other room IDs return unchanged.

Requires overlap with object $67. In room $5E shows message $0B, moves cage fields, hides sprites, runs the celebration and message $0C. Else checks coin tens against three: three shows message $0E and returns to title, other counts show message $0D.

For rooms below $19, computes $4000+A*64, reads 63 bytes in ascending order, reverses their bits through $A400 and stores them in descending order at $4A80. Returns sprite pointer $2A. Rooms at least $19 return without conversion.
When the sound toggle and animation parity allow and movement state is below two, writes a short noise voice on SID voice 1, volume nine, alternating frequency high bytes six and ten.
RTS ending the footstep effect. The row-shift code names this address as one byte before its actual buffer, then indexes it from one upward.
Thirty-two-byte scratch allocation for a source bitmap row, its mirrored bytes and the additional nibble-shift carry byte.
Number of shape-$73 scenery entries recorded for the room, with a limit of ten in the renderer.
Ten X-coordinate slots for the animated shape-$73 scenery list.
Ten Y-coordinate slots paired with the animated X list at $2B14.
Ten drawing-attribute slots paired with the scenery X/Y lists; animation flips their mirror bit.
Sets the KERNAL IRQ vector $0314 to $2B49, clears the sound selector and sound toggle, and enables interrupts.
Counter incremented by the music IRQ. Low bits equal to seven suppress that interrupt's music call.
Main-loop sound mode flag toggled by keyboard code $24; selects background music versus the footstep effect path.
Increments $2B47, masks its low three bits and skips the music call when those bits equal seven. Otherwise calls $0B01, then chains to KERNAL $EA31.

Takes shape A and coordinates $033A/$033B, attribute $033C and collision flags $033F. Rejects X at least $5D, resolves the shape header, records animated scenery, computes bitmap, colour and collision-plane pointers, clips horizontal output, and draws rows. Digits and letters $30-$5A force one byte by eight rows. Supports mirroring, a four-pixel horizontal shift and self-modified load/XOR/OR composition.

The renderer patches this instruction to load source pixels directly or XOR/OR them with the destination byte. Writes the clipped row, updates colour and collision attributes once per character row, advances the source and bitmap pointers and stops at the height or lower clip boundary. The operand byte $2CF6 is part of the patched instruction.

Operand byte of the compositor at $2CF5: $EA produces LDA $EAEA,Y and $FB selects the existing bitmap pointer for ORA/EOR. The following code stores pixels, colour and collision attributes and advances to the next source row.
Moves each byte's low nibble into the following byte's high nibble through the row buffer at $2AF3, adds a cleared carry byte and extends the horizontal draw limit when the result fits.

Maps the low three attribute bits through $1897 to the cell colour, combines collision flags from attribute bits 5 and 6, and rewrites $2CF5-$2CF6 to select a load, XOR or OR against the existing destination pixel byte.
Reverses the row buffer's byte order while replacing each byte with its bit reversal from $A400. Handles an odd central byte separately.

Rejects room IDs at least $65. Uses consecutive little-endian offsets at $8000 plus base $80CC to delimit a room stream. Each record gives shape, X and Y; X bit 7 reuses the previous attribute, otherwise a fourth byte supplies attribute XOR $40. Draws each record through $2B5B until the stream end.
Draws the room name and lives panel. If object five remains present, resets two live object fields, then falls through to the room redraw.

Resets room animation counters, disables sprites, clears the list of animated scenery, sets room-dependent moving objects, clears the playfield and draws room scenery. Adds conditional overlays in rooms $24 and $3A and a vertical strip in room $33. Draws live objects, sets up room-specific strips and composes colours before enabling sprites.

Clears the interior bitmap and screen buffers for character rows six through 22, gives the secondary colour buffer $10, and clears $5800-$59FF. Leaves the status header and side frame outside the interior writes.

For rows six through 22 and columns five through 34, uses the collision/attribute plane's low three bits as a colour lookup when nonzero, otherwise copies the saved room colour. Writes the composed screen matrix.

Checks four room IDs against $18E8 and live attributes, copies initial Y bounds for matching strips into live tables and repeatedly draws them while advancing Y. Room $5E has an additional strip drawn from Y=$C50C[$65] up to $66 when $C894 differs from five.
With X as slot, clears its software X/Y positions and two state arrays, then writes the slot to VIC through $31EE.

Computes a probe at player X plus $033A minus one and player Y plus $033B plus $27. Resolves bitmap and attribute row pointers, reads one nibble from the collision plane and returns it in A; carry records attribute bit $40. Stores probe coordinates and masks in scratch bytes.
Busy delay with A outer iterations of an X countdown from 255. Saves A at $0340 and restores X through $0345. A zero outer count wraps through 256 iterations; interrupts remain enabled.
Uses slot $034E, doubles its software X, updates that slot's bit of $D010, and writes X and Y to the VIC. X outside $1C-$90 and Y outside $4A-$E5 become zero. Preserves X and Y through scratch bytes.
Increments eight-bit index $03C5 and reads a KERNAL ROM byte at $E290+index into A and $03C6. Preserves X.
Increments eight-bit index $03C5, reads a KERNAL ROM byte at $EA60+index, masks two bits and adds one. Returns 1 through 4 in A and $03C6, preserving X.
With A as direction bits and slot $034E, moves Y up or down by $037A[slot] and X left or right by $0384[slot]. Hides slots whose X is $E6-$F2 or whose Y falls below eight.
Loads live object X and Y, clears colour and drawing flags, and draws its shape through $2B5B.
Loads an object's live X, Y, attribute and shape from the parallel tables at $C724, $C7AA, $C830 and $C8B6, draws it, then restores destination offset $58.

Scans all 134 live objects in descending order and draws those whose room matches $03E5. For IDs below $3F, combines per-object colour with the global mask and checks initial room/X/Y to mark moved objects. Leaves the scan index reset to $86 and mask $FF.
Returns $FF=$08 unless the global mask is nonzero and the object's room, X and Y still match the three initial tables, in which case returns $FF=0. Leaves other registers as scratch.

Inverts joystick port 2 at $DC00 and masks five bits, merges keyboard controls, then suppresses action bit $10 while it was present in the previous sample. Stores the result at $03C0 and the preceding sample at $03D8.

Converts player coordinates to VIC coordinates, hides slots two through five, sets their colour, sprite pointer and X/Y speeds, then places them at the four corners of a rectangle whose half-width is A and half-height A/2.
Advances sprite slots 2 through 5 using their direction and speed tables, updates VIC registers, then delays eight units. Repeats this group five times.

Restores the saved room-entry coordinates, creates four particles around the player, steps the player's appearance frames through three particle groups, clears movement and spare sprite slots and drains the VIC collision latches.

Creates particles at the player's position, selects sound four and runs ten particle groups while advancing player sprite frames. Clears all eight sprite slots, delays 100 units and restores the saved room ID.
Combines KERNAL key code $C5 and shift flags $028D with $03C0. Key codes $0C and $17 add left and right bits, any shift adds jump, and code $01 adds action. Returns the sampled key code in Y.
Disables interrupts and banks all RAM in with $01=$34, reads through $05/$06 and advances that pointer, restores $01=$36 and enables interrupts. Returns the byte in A.

Selects a text stream from the pointer table at $D148 with A as message ID. Bytes >=$FB end it; $FA draws a box, $C8-$F9 set colour, $64-$C7 set X followed by Y, and $5F waits for a fresh action press. Other bytes become shapes $26-$5A, with out-of-range bytes drawn as shape $3A. Advances X by two per character and redraws the room after a non-title message ends at a doubled $5F.

Reads width and interior height from the text stream, hides hardware sprites, and draws the four corners, horizontal borders and interior rows through $36E3. Uses $0398/$0399 as the dimensions and moves the text cursor inside the box.
Draws one horizontal box border using shapes $2A, $2E, repeated $28, $2E and $2B, advancing by two X units per shape and eight Y units per row.
Advances Y by eight and draws shape $29 at each side with $0398 copies of blank shape $3A between them.
Draws shape A at text cursor $039A/$039C with colour $03BF, zero collision flags and zero drawing offset, then advances the cursor X by two.

If the inventory list begins nonzero, selects the name pointer for object A from $D0CA, except object four with $C834=1 uses $D1C0. Reads through the banked text reader and draws bytes $26-$5A until another byte ends the name.
Fills the five-byte inventory list at $18D9 with $FF, scans object IDs 1 through 62 for live room four, appends their IDs and terminates with zero.
Rebuilds the inventory list, chooses message $37 or $38 depending on whether object zero is carried, and draws each carried object's name in rows eight pixels apart. An empty list shows message $3B.
For room IDs below $65, reads the name pointer from RAM at $D000+2*room, sets X=$2C and Y=$18 and draws characters until $5F. Disables interrupts around reads beneath I/O and KERNAL.
Draws two egg shapes at X=$2E and $30, Y=8. Each slot before spare-life count $03B9 uses colour six; later slots use colour zero. Shape $2F supplies the egg.

Clears the playfield, selects sound four, then draws 256 pseudo-random letters at pseudo-random X and Y positions, delaying five units after each. Shape selection maps random result four to one before adding $1C.
Takes shape index in $FB, doubles it and indexes the pointer-offset table at $A500, adding $A7 to the fetched high byte. Returns its data address in $B4/$B5.

On alternating passes, animates a marked horizontal scenery strip using shapes $5C-$5F and collision flag $10. Erases and redraws alternating subsets of the stored shape-$73 list, flipping their horizontal mirror bit each time. Uses $2B13 as the stored list count.

Accepts selected object IDs $1A-$37, marks the object's room $FF and clears the selection, increments decimal coin units at $18E6 with carry to tens $18E5, selects sound three and redraws the counter. Shows message $36 and restores sound two when the sound toggle is clear.

With X as object ID, rejects objects outside the current room, resolves the shape's width and height, and checks strict rectangle overlap with player rectangle X=$0352+$21 through +4 and Y=$035C+$2A through +21. Returns carry set on overlap, clear otherwise.
Draws the tens and units at X=$4E/$50, Y=8 in colour six using shape $30 plus each decimal digit.
Maps colour A through $1897 and fills 22 bytes of the selected inventory row, starting at offset nine. Object zero being carried moves the list's first row up by one.

Draws shape $70 on alternating X positions from the active breath length through length+8, clipped to $32-$43. Uses object $71's Y and colour six for the portion before the endpoint, zero after it, then redraws object $72.
KERNAL key codes $0E,$0D,$29,$21,$2A,$14,$0E: E S P I L C E. The room browser checks them in order and waits for each key to change.
Sixteen direction-mask entries used by the room browser. Single directions add +16, -16, -1 or +1; combinations with zero entries leave the room unchanged.

Compares seven successive KERNAL key codes against $3AE9, requiring release after each. On success hides sprites, restores spare lives to two, draws the lives panel and permits room selection with joystick directions using signed steps at $3AF0. Accepts room IDs $15-$A7; action exits and reenables sprites.
Retained text-mode restore routine: selects VIC bank zero, text mode, screen/charset pointer $15 and processor port $37, then returns. The traced game startup selects bitmap video instead.
Selects VIC bank $4000, bitmap mode with screen at $5C00 and bitmap at $6000, black border, clipping Y=$30 through $B7, and drawing destination offset $58.
